anchors: Pin each decision with a test that fails when the decision is reverted
decision: A jig records each choice a later editor could undo in a Decisions block in its module docstring, every entry pinned by a test that fails when the decision is reverted, and the block is read before a matcher, rule or threshold changes.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: hooks, jigs and scripts keep their reason in a Decisions block in the module docstring plus a regression test that goes red when the decision is reverted; no new file and no new gate for code

reopen_if: A jig decision is undone although its docstring entry and pinning test both carried it, or editors keep missing the block.
why: Jig rules were changed forward and back because the reason sat in a commit or a changelog the next editor never reads; the module and its tests are what that editor opens.

decision: Rejected: a decisions.jsonl ledger for hooks and jigs.

evidence.text: user decision 2026-11-05: skills get the ledger, code keeps its reason in the module docstring and a regression test; no new file and no new gate for code

reopen_if: a reverted code decision is found whose docstring and tests both carried it and it was still undone
why: code already carries its reason in the module docstring and its behaviour in a regression test; a second record would drift from both

decision: Not adopted: documenting where ci_wait's CI_RC= line lands when ci_wait runs as a backgrounded Bash call.
reopen_if: ci_wait.py starts printing a CI_RC= line or another fixed verdict line whose location a caller has to know.
why: Refuted: ci_wait.py prints no CI_RC= line (its verdict goes to stdout on success, to stderr otherwise). The line that went missing was the caller's own echo, written outside the redirect.

decision: Not adopted: rewording gate.py's --help line on --name, reported as contradicting the parser's refusal '--name must be written AFTER the --gate it labels'.
reopen_if: gate.py's help and its parser come to disagree on where --name goes, or the same line is misread again.
why: No contradiction: the help says a --name labels the --gate written before it, which is the rule the parser enforces. The report misread the help.

anchors: since `--ref` resolves in that `--repo` directory, else in the current directory's repo
decision: ci_wait --ref resolves in the --repo directory when --repo names a local checkout, else (no --repo, or OWNER/NAME) in the current repo; the skill says so in the ci_wait row and in the no-runs checklist.

evidence.text: tests/test_ci_wait.py::TestRefOnTheCommandLine::test_a_ref_is_resolved_inside_a_directory_repo_not_the_cwd fails on the pre-fix script and passes after; opus and haiku probes on the pre-edit text answered the cwd's HEAD, on the new text the worktree's HEAD, quoting it.

reopen_if: ci_wait stops resolving --ref in a --repo directory, or starts resolving it for an OWNER/NAME --repo some other way.
why: Run from the main checkout with --repo naming a linked worktree, --ref HEAD resolved in the cwd and reported the main checkout's verdict as the worktree's, a green for the wrong sha. The tool now resolves in the --repo directory, and text saying 'the current repo' would steer a reader to cd needlessly or to distrust a correct run.
